newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Liberalisation fuels Asia insurance demand - report.
newsitem.headline: Liberalisation fuels Asia insurance demand - report.

text.p: Liberalisation of insurance regulations in Asia and global competition will fuel demand for new products and underwriting capacity in the region, according to a report received by Reuters on Wednesday.
"As this (liberalising) trend continues, so will the need for new insurance products and services, as well as greater blocks of capacity," said the 162-page report from U.S. broker Johnson & Higgins.

While the report was optimistic about the long-term opportunities for insurers in Asia, it stressed that progress would require perseverance as liberalisation occurred at varying paces in different countries.
The report gave views on prospects in Japan, China, South Korea, Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Cambodia, Burma and Laos) and Thailand.

The report's authors said they were doubtful that change in Japan would occur quickly despite the passing of an insurance law in 1996 to facilitate deregulation and the resolution of the U.S.-Japanese insurance trade row.
"It is likely to take 10 years for reform to be fully implemented," the report said.
In China, the report saw massive opportunity, but said there were huge hurdles for foreign firms planning a presence as new licences would be limited to one or two a year.

South Korea offered some of the best prospects, the report said. Already the sixth biggest insurance market in the world, the report said it would evolve "to match worldwide insurance practices and standards".
The report said the sector's performance in Southeast Asia would vary between countries, but would generally be characterised by further expansion and liberalisation.
